claim: `openSession` narrows on `end-time`, which sits in the stretch rows rather than on the day page, so the ask cannot be scoped before the read and every call opens the sessions file of every day Alan has tracked. `safety-reading` and `cost-reading` both call it on five-minute timers. `sessionsOfDay` was scoped in the same module and fell from 84 files to 1; `openSession` still pays the whole folder.

evidence:
`openSession` in `alan/track/daily/modules/day-stretches/day-stretches.module.code.ts` asks with `where: { "end-time": { empty: true } }` and hands no `ofDay`, so `sessionsAnswered` builds a query with no day-level `where`.

`bodyTests` in `page/service/modules/kinds-gathering/kinds-gathering.module.code.ts` keeps only the tests answerable from the page's own body, and withholds every key declared by a `page-property-entry`. `end-time` is such a key, held in `day-<date>.day.sessions.jsonl`, so the test runs only after the file is opened.

Measured on this workstation after the narrowing landed: the unnarrowed ask reads 84 sessions files and 292,779 bytes and takes 1.78 s per 40 calls; the day-narrowed ask reads 1 file and 3,195 bytes and takes 0.44 s.

Scoping this needs a day-level fact saying which day holds the open session, because no key on the day page carries it today.
